2026

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Binod Kumar Dwivedi
 On The 6 th Of April, 2026
 Misc. Appeal No. 2143 of 2014
 United India Insurance Co.Ltd.
 Versus
 Smt.Sangeeta Bai And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Pradip Kumar Gupta - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Vijay Singh Chouhan - Advocate for respondents n
 Order

This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant/Insurance Company assailing the impugned award dated 29.08.2014 passed by Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sonkatch, district Dewas (M.P.) in Claim Case No.55/2013, whereby an amount of Rs.19,50,489/- has been awarded to the survivors of the deceased Ravi Kumar, aged about 30 years, Panchayat Secretary by profession who passed away in a road traffic accident which occurred on 05.11.2012.
2.

Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the accident took place on 05.11.2012,
but the FIR was lodged on 19.11.2012 by delay of 14 days which in itself reveals that this is a case of false implication on the cooked up story.
The evidence was available in this regard which has not been properly appreciated by the Claims Tribunal.

Hence, prays for NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:8865 2 MA-2143-2014 allowing the appeal by setting aside the direction for payment of the award amount by the Insurance Company.

He also opposed the cross objection filed on behalf of the claimants/respondents for enhancement of the award amount on the ground that the income as proved by salary certificate Ex.P-177 to the effect of Rs.6,438/- has been properly taken for assessing the just and proper compensation and prays for dismissing the cross objection.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants, survivors of the deceased submits that mere delay in lodging the FIR cannot be a ground to assume that this is case of false implication.
He further submits that the evidence is available by way of record of the criminal case which has been properly proved and the Insurance Company has not led any evidence in rebuttal.
Hence the finding of Claims Tribunal that this is a case of false implication cannot be disturbed.

He further submits that the income has not been properly assessed which as resulted in awarding lower amount of United India Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Smt.Sangeeta Bai on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166125883/
1 compensation.

sentences.text: Therefore, prays for allowing the cross objection by dismissing the appeal of the Insurance Company.

4. Heard and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.
It is not in dispute that mere delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to assume that it is a case of false implication.
The evidence made available by the claimants which is documentary as well as oral evidence has not been rebutted by the Insurance Company.
Hence, the objection raised by the Insurance Company with regard to false implication of the vehicle is meritless.

As far as the cross objection raised on behalf of the claimants, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8865 3 MA-2143-2014 survivors of the deceased is concerned, this Court is of the view that the salary certificate Ex.P-177 reveals that the income of the deceased Ravi Kumar as Rs.6,438/- has been taken into account by the Claims Tribunal.
As per his age 30 years, 50% has been taken as future prospects.
Other heads has been properly addressed.
No ground is made out that the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation amount on the lower side.
6. Resultantly, this appeal filed by the Insurance Company and the Cross Objection filed by the survivors of the deceased are found baseless.
Hence, the appeal as well as the Cross Objection are dismissed.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE RJ United India Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Smt.Sangeeta Bai on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166125883/
